messages:
jane-cust: Hey team — we've been seeing a regression for streaming responses from the hosted API since last deploy. TTFB looks okay (~150-400ms) but p99 total latency is spiking to 8–12s for long outputs. Non-streaming calls to the same model have much lower p99 (under 1s). Request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. Using node-fetch in our app with http2 enabled. Can we get help reproducing / mitigations?

alex: sorry you're hitting this, thanks for the details. Can you share a minimal repro curl and the exact headers you use for streaming? also which model + max_tokens?

jane-cust: sure — model: redwood-2-small, max_tokens: 512, streaming=true. curl we used (http2):

```bash
curl -v -N --http2 \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","prompt":"<long prompt>","stream":true}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

We also tried node-fetch:

```js
const res = await fetch(url, {method: 'POST', headers, body});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
// we log timings when first chunk arrives and when stream ends
```

Measured timings: first chunk ~300ms, but last chunk at ~8.3s for a 400-token response (unexpected).

alex: thanks, that timing gap is strange. @mira / @jorge can you take a look? could be proxy/coalescing or client buffering.

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-04-26T15:12:03 completed on infra-blue, runtime v3.11.1

mira: thx — quick notes: runtime does adaptive coalescing based on avg token size and flush interval. Usually streaming shows TTFB as first chunk and then steady small chunks. The pattern you describe (fast first chunk + long quiet tail) usually indicates either: (a) upstream connection multiplexing/flow-control stall (http2 window) or (b) an intermediary proxy/buffer waiting for a chunk boundary (newline or double-newline) before flushing to client.

jorge: adding that I've seen cloud proxies (some customers behind custom CDN gateways) buffer until 16KB or newline. Do you know if you're behind any edge/proxy? Also which region — us-west1?

jane-cust: yes us-west1, and we are behind our infra team’s edge (they said a lightweight proxy for auth). We tested bypassing it by hitting the api directly from a workstation and still saw the same behaviour, though slightly better (p99 ~4.5s).

mira: good repro — that suggests there are multiple contributors. Two engineering suggestions we can try right away:
1) send explicit flush-friendly markers from the server (e.g. ensure chunks end with "\n\n" or a boundary) to force many proxies to flush immediately. We already send newline in many spots but might be missing for some tokens.
2) for immediate customer relief: toggle the server-side coalescing window down for your tenant only (reduces server-side batching so more frequent smaller chunks). That is low-risk but increases per-token overhead.

alex: @maja any billing impact if we enable tenant-level low-coalesce fallback? customer wants to avoid surprise bills.

maja: enabling lower coalescing will slightly increase token-related compute + network egress, but should not change pricing model — usage still billed per token. We'll add a short note to the customer's billing profile and email if we flip it so they are aware.

jane-cust: ok to try the tenant toggle, would appreciate it. Also can you share a recommended client-side pattern so we don't rely on proxies flushing?

mira: client-side: prefer a streaming reader that processes chunks incrementally and doesn't wait for "\n\n". For Node fetch: use `response.body.getReader()` and pump the stream; for browsers use `ReadableStreamDefaultReader`. Example: 

```js
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let t0 = Date.now();
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  // immediate processing - don't buffer into big string
  processChunk(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
  console.log('chunk at', Date.now() - t0);
}
```

Also consider SSE mode (Accept: text/event-stream) if your client stacks treat that specially.

jorge: on the infra side I'll check if the proxy is doing http2 multiplexing and what the window sizes look like. If the proxy is holding frames until a threshold, that explains desktop->direct improvement but still bad p99. I'll run a tcpdump for a repro window — Jane, can you run the repro at 15:30 PDT today so we have aligned traces?

jane-cust: yes we can. we'll run the exact curl and node script at 15:30.

mira: follow-up mitigation plan (short term):
- Flip tenant coalesce to aggressive-flush for 24h (targeted ramp) — reduces internal batching.
- Add optional response header `x-redwood-force-flush: true` that clients can set to request more frequent flushes (we'll gate this to trusted customers).
- Engineering to instrument chunk flush timestamps in traces so we can tell whether stall is on server, proxy, or client.

alex: I'll file an internal incident to track this and set the owner. Action items:
- @mira do tenant toggle and add instrumentation (ETA 2h).
- @jorge validate proxy traces once customer runs repro (ETA 3h).
- @maja send billing heads-up if toggle flips (before toggle).
- @jane-cust run repro at 15:30 and paste curl timings here.

mira: started tenant toggle (jackpot mode -> aggressive flush) for tenant r-0a1b2c3d. I'll roll it back if we see cost or stability issues.

jorge: prepping the packet capture window — will share a secure link for pcap upload.

jane-cust: repro run done. timings: first chunk 320ms, intermittent chunks ~50–120ms for ~200ms, then a 6.9s stall, then remaining chunks. Uploaded pcap to the link. logs: request-id still r-0a1b2c3d.

mira: looking at traces — server emitted chunks steadily, the server-side chunk timestamps show no 6–7s gap. The gap appears after the egress point — proxy delayed a series of frames and then flushed them. That matches buffering behavior.

alex: thanks for the quick turnaround. Jane — we'll keep the tenant toggle on for 24h, and if your app validates improved p99 we'll keep it and look at a longer-term fix (maybe automated flush negotiation or smaller default coalesce for streaming endpoints).

jane-cust: seeing much better p99 now after the toggle (~900ms). thanks all. :relieved:

mira: great — we still want to harden for other customers: follow-ups: add per-chunk flush header, improve server-side instrumentation, and document recommended proxy configs (disable large-buffering for streaming endpoints).

alex: closing loop here — marking this resolved for now, will leave notes in ticket and ping if regression recurs. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
